root_cause.text: Off-by-one bounds checks in the Rockchip rkcif MIPI register lookup helpers (`rkcif_mipi_get_reg()` and `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg()`) used `>` instead of `>=`, allowing `block`, `id`, or `index` values equal to the array length to pass and cause out-of-bounds array access in the MIPI `blocks`, `regs`, and `regs_id` tables.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `block > ...`, `id > ...`, and `index > ...` to `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, `id >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and `index >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says this is to “avoid accessing one element beyond the end of the arrays.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: Off-by-one bounds checks in the Rockchip rkcif MIPI register lookup helpers (`rkcif_mipi_get_reg()` and `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg()`) used `>` instead of `>=`, allowing `block`, `id`, or `index` values equal to the array length to pass and cause out-of-bounds array access in the MIPI `blocks`, `regs`, and `regs_id` tables.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `block > ...`, `id > ...`, and `index > ...` to `block >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, `id >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and `index >= ARRAY_SIZE(...)`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says this is to “avoid accessing one element beyond the end of the arrays.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten rkcif_mipi_get_reg() bounds checking to use actual MIPI array sizes and prevent out-of-range accesses.
intent_record.what: The bounds checks in rkcif_mipi_get_reg() were changed from comparing block and index against fixed maximum constants using '>' to comparing them against the runtime array sizes of rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks and rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs using '>=' and ARRAY_SIZE().
intent_record.how: This makes the function reject out-of-range block and register indices based on the actual backing array lengths, including the previous boundary-equal case, preventing invalid array access and returning RKCIF_REGISTER_NOTSUPPORTED when the indices are not supported.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix MIPI register index validation by checking against actual array sizes to prevent out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: The change replaces three hard-coded upper-bound WARN_ON_ONCE checks using `>` against constants (`RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE`, `RKCIF_ID_MAX`, and `RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX`) with bounds checks using `>= ARRAY_SIZE(...)` on the actual `mipi->blocks`, `mipi->regs_id`, and `mipi->regs_id[id]` arrays.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now validates `block`, `id`, and `index` against the real sizes of the backing arrays instead of separate maximum constants, preventing out-of-bounds access when an index is equal to or larger than the array length and keeping the function returning `RKCIF_REGISTER_NOTSUPPORTED` for unsupported values.

grouping_result.intent: Tighten rkcif_mipi_get_reg() bounds checking to use actual MIPI array sizes and prevent out-of-range accesses.
Fix MIPI register index validation by checking against actual array sizes to prevent out-of-bounds access.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by tightening bounds checks in rkcif_mipi_get_reg() to use correct array sizes and prevent out-of-range/OOB access from off-by-one validation errors.

The group directly fixes the MIPI register index bounds checks to use correct array-size validation, preventing the same out-of-bounds accesses caused by the off-by-one `>` vs `>=` bug in the lookup helpers.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check is off by one: using > allows block equal to the number of MIPI blocks to pass, leading to out-of-bounds access when indexing the blocks array.
This index validation is off by one: using > instead of >= permits index equal to the register table length, enabling out-of-bounds access into the regs table.
This off-by-one check lets block equal to the array length through in the ID-based helper, causing out-of-bounds indexing of the blocks table.
This off-by-one validation allows id equal to the regs_id dimension size, which can cause out-of-bounds access into the regs_id table.
This off-by-one check allows index equal to the regs_id entry count, permitting out-of-bounds access in the regs_id table.

vuln_statements.explanation: This off-by-one bounds check uses > instead of >= for block validation, allowing a block value equal to the table length to pass and leading to out-of-bounds access of the MIPI blocks array.
This off-by-one bounds check uses > instead of >= for the register index, permitting index equal to the regs table length and causing out-of-bounds access in rkcif_mipi_get_reg().

This off-by-one bounds check uses > instead of >= for id validation, allowing id equal to the regs_id dimension size to pass and causing out-of-bounds access in the ID-based MIPI register lookup helper.
This off-by-one bounds check uses > instead of >= for the ID-register index, allowing index equal to the regs_id entry count and enabling out-of-bounds access into the regs_id table.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:

Author: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@collabora.com>

    media: rockchip: rkcif: add support for rk3568 vicap mipi capture
    
    The RK3568 Video Capture (VICAP) unit features a MIPI CSI-2 capture
    interface. Add support for the MIPI capture interface in general
    and for the RK3568 VICAP MIPI capture in particular.
    
    Signed-off-by: Michael Riesch <michael.riesch@wolfvision.net>
    Reviewed-b
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly contains the two relevant helper functions and their bounds checks, so it is sufficient to assess the off-by-one issue. In `rkcif_mipi_get_reg()`, the check is `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) || WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_REGISTER_MAX))`, followed by array accesses `rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks[block].offset` and `rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs[index]`. Because the checks use `>` instead of `>=`, a `block` or `index` value equal to the array limit would pass and then be used as an array index, matching the described root cause. Likewise, in `rkcif_mipi_id_get_reg()`, the check is `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(block > RKCIF_MIPI_MAX - RKCIF_MIPI_BASE) || WARN_ON_ONCE(id > RKCIF_ID_MAX) || WARN_ON_ONCE(index > RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX))`, followed by `rkcif->match_data->mipi->blocks[block].offset` and `rkcif->match_data->mipi->regs_id[id][index]`. Again, `>` allows `block == limit`, `id == RKCIF_ID_MAX`, or `index == RKCIF_MIPI_ID_REGISTER_MAX` to pass, creating the out-of-bounds condition. The fix would require `>=` style checks (or equivalent length-safe validation), which is not present here.
